I'm thankful for all the optimists. Americans are a profoundly optimistic bunch, and I think it's one of the things you really appreciate and are drawn to as an immigrant.

In order to define the future and lead the world, you must possess a positive vision of what's to come.

keywords.definition_zh: 「total addressable market」的缩写，指产品或服务理论上能够覆盖的整体市场规模。
keywords.example_zh: 作者认为，交付能力提升后，服务公司有机会服务过去未纳入目标市场的小客户。

tweets.text:
Huge opportunity right now to build new services firms from the ground up, or transform existing ones, with agents at the center. 

The expertise that services firms in theory should have is as important as ever because you still need deep domain understanding to get the most out of agents. But now the ability to deliver on projects has a 10X multiplier. This means that you can make clients happier, compete to win more of them, go after smaller customers not in the TAM before, or deliver outcomes that weren’t really conceivable.

This is going to happen in advertising, IT transformation, management consulting, finance, and a number of other fields that historically are just fully constrained by the speed of their workforce for output. 

This is a huge opportunity right now for those starting these firms. I wouldn’t count out existing players that commit to the transformation either as existing customer trust goes a long way. But they have to move quickly to make it work.
tweets.summary_en: AI agents could let services firms deliver projects much faster, serve smaller clients, and take on work that was previously impractical. Deep domain expertise still matters, and established firms can build on client trust if they adapt quickly.

tweets.text:
12 tips for people who posted on LinkedIn but now wanna post on X

A lot of people I know are moving their posting from LinkedIn to X. When they ask me how I grew 80k followers on X in one year, here’s what I tell them:

1. LinkedIn is a stage. X is a party. First you find your crowd, then you listen to what they're already talking about. Don't start talking until you get it

2. You can't reach the C-suite directly. LinkedIn is a professional network, so you can go straight to decision makers. X doesn't work like that. You have to get mass attention first, and then the right people notice you

3. Post way more than you think. On LinkedIn, 3-5 posts a week counts as a lot. I posted 3 times a day on X for 6 months. Some founders I follow post 5 times a day. It's not that they're on X all day. They just don't overthink it

4. Make posting a reflex. If you spend too long on a post, you won't post. Whenever a thought comes up, post it right there. No planning, no scheduling, no waiting for the right time

5. It's a numbers game. Most posts won't do well. Maybe 1 in 10 will. Maybe 1 in 50 goes viral. That's normal

6. Half your posts should be reactions. LinkedIn is mostly “proactive content”. On X, at least at the start, half of what you post should be “reactive content”: replies, quote tweets, commentary on what others already said

7. Know the difference between a reply and a quote tweet. A reply is like a LinkedIn DM. It says "notice me." A quote tweet uses someone else's content to grow your own account

8. Fix your feed first. If you wanna talk about cybersecurity and your feed is all politics, you can't join the right conversations. Pick a few big names in your niche. See who they follow and who they engage with, and follow those people too. Like, bookmark and comment. After about a week your timeline will look totally different

9. Write like you're texting an acquaintance. Polish turns people off. Everyone's allergic to perfect AI-sounding writing. And please don't use AI or bots to write your replies. People can tell, and they might block you

10. Post the stuff that's obvious to you. Make a list of the top 10 questions customers, investors and your team ask you. That's where you're the expert. What seems too obvious to talk about is exactly what people want to hear

11. Post what you just said out loud. If you say something in real life and people go "huh, never thought of it that way," post it on your way back. Don't wait, you'll forget. You don't have to block out time to think of what to say. Just say what you've already said

12. Show your face, and don't sell yet. X is a wall of text, so video stands out. I just record myself on my laptop with something on the screen. People wanna know you're a real human, not AI slop. And until you have about 1,000 followers, don't promote your company. Share real opinions first. Later, when you repost company news, always add your own take, not PR speak.

Remember: people follow people, not companies
tweets.summary_en: To grow on X after posting on LinkedIn, find your community, listen to its conversations, and post frequently without overthinking. Use replies to get noticed by individuals and quote posts to reach a broader audience.

tweets.text:
I am thankful for a lot of things in life, but my family is the best thing that has ever happened to me.

The two most common things people said to me before having kids is that it's better than anyone can explain to you and it goes very fast; these are both true and I don't have much to add. But I am very grateful and I love them more than there is any way to explain.

Also I cannot really imagine life without Ollie and I think without his unwavering support and great advice I would have gone crazy by now.

🦃
tweets.summary_en: Parenthood has brought more joy than words can capture, and the time with young children passes quickly. The post also expresses gratitude for Ollie's steady support and advice.

tweets.text:
Ven was one of the earliest believers that we could use our then-current model to solve millenium prize problems.

There are a lot of brilliant people in the world, but being brilliant and also having correctly-placed confidence and courage to keep pushing on something that others don't think is possible is a very valuable thing and fairly rare.

I am grateful so many people at OpenAI have this combination.
tweets.summary_en: Ven believed early that OpenAI's model at the time could solve Millennium Prize Problems. The post praises the rare combination of brilliance, sound judgment about what's possible, and the courage to pursue it despite skepticism.

tweets.text:
Oh, one thing about kids:

Most good things get a little less satisfying the 100th time you do them.

A quiet evening hanging out with your kids, even doing very mundane stuff, is in the rare category of something repetitive just getting better and better.

vocab.definition_en: Likely to split people into groups with strongly opposing views.
vocab.example_en: Giving AI agents permission to spend money is a divisive idea.
vocab.example_zh: 允许 AI 智能体花钱是个容易引起强烈分歧的想法。

vocab.definition_en: To establish something again or give an existing organization a fresh start.
vocab.definition_zh: 重新创立，也可指让现有组织从根本上重新出发。
vocab.example_en: The team wanted to refound the company around a simpler mission.
vocab.example_zh: 团队希望围绕一个更简单的使命重塑公司。

vocab.definition_en: An established company or provider that already holds a position in a market.
vocab.definition_zh: 已经在某个市场占有一席之地的公司或服务商。
vocab.example_en: The startup won customers from the incumbent by making its product easier to use.
vocab.example_zh: 这家初创公司把产品做得更易用，从老牌竞争对手那里赢得了客户。

vocab.definition_en: A person or group expected to lose a contest or struggle.
vocab.definition_zh: 在竞争中处于劣势、通常不被看好的一方。
vocab.example_en: Fans rallied behind the underdog after its surprise win.
vocab.example_zh: 这支不被看好的队伍意外获胜后，球迷纷纷站出来支持它。

vocab.definition_en: Provided by or made possible by someone or something, sometimes said jokingly.
vocab.definition_zh: 由某人或某机构提供，也可用来调侃某件事是「拜……所赐」。
vocab.example_en: The demo is online, courtesy of a teammate who stayed late to deploy it.
vocab.example_zh: 多亏一位队友加班完成部署，演示版已经上线了。

vocab.definition_en: Deeply or to a very great degree.
vocab.definition_zh: 深刻地，非常，程度很深地。
vocab.example_en: She was profoundly optimistic about what her team could build.
vocab.example_zh: 她对团队能做出什么成果充满信心。

vocab.definition_en: Naturally attracted to or interested in someone or something.
vocab.definition_zh: 被某人或某事吸引，自然而然地产生兴趣。
vocab.example_en: I was drawn to the team because people could speak openly about their mistakes.
vocab.example_zh: 这支团队吸引我，是因为大家都能坦诚地谈论自己的错误。

quote.text_en: A better future begins with the courage to imagine it and the patience to build it.
quote.text_zh: 更好的未来，始于敢于想象的勇气，也需要一步步把它建成的耐心。
quote.author: Original

slang_glossary.definition_en: Payments initiated or managed by an AI agent acting on a user's behalf.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 由 AI 智能体代表用户发起或管理的支付。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Enter an emerging market or start using a technology before it becomes widely adopted.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在市场或技术普及之前提早入场。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Handle something well or make the right choices about how it should work.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 把某件事做对，或在关键设计和决策上把握得当。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Rebuild or redefine an existing company while openly sharing decisions and inviting outside feedback.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 公开重塑一家现有公司，同时分享决策并听取外部反馈。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Show the real people behind an organization or issue so it feels more relatable.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 让幕后的人走到台前，让机构或议题更有亲切感。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A formal, carefully managed tone that people associate with large companies.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 让人联想到大公司的正式、经过精心包装的调性。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An established company or provider already operating in a market.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 已在市场占有一席之地的厂商或服务商。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A story framed around a person or organization facing stronger rivals and unlikely odds.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 围绕弱势一方挑战强劲对手展开的故事。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A wry way to say that reactions on Twitter may be unrepresentative of the people who matter to a business or issue.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 一种调侃，意思是推特上的反应未必代表真实客户或更广泛人群的看法。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Someone whose online presence or reputation can shape other people's opinions or choices.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 能凭借线上影响力或声誉左右他人看法和选择的人。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Share ideas while they are still taking shape so others can react and contribute.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在想法尚未成熟时就公开分享，让别人参与讨论和反馈。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Stay within the Overton window, the range of ideas considered publicly acceptable in a given context.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 把观点保持在「奥弗顿窗口」内，也就是特定环境下公众能够接受的范围内。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The starting point of a project, release, or launch.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 项目、发布或上线刚开始的那一天。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Is running and available to use, often said of a newly launched feature or service.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 已上线并可使用，常用于刚推出的功能或服务。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An unexplained label in the sample. The post says it is online, but does not identify what it refers to.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 样本中未解释的名称。原文只说它已上线，具体指什么无从判断。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A unit of ownership in a company, as in a share of SpaceX.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 代表公司一部分所有权的股份，例如「一股 SpaceX 股票」。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Put on a mask or face covering.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 戴上口罩或其他遮住面部的物品。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A type of lock-opening tool mentioned in the game's context.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 游戏语境中提到的一种开锁工具。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Open a lock without its key by manipulating the lock mechanism.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 不用原配钥匙，通过拨动锁具内部机构来开锁。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The combination or passcode for a safe.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 保险柜的开启密码。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Short for Grand Theft Auto VI, the video game referenced in the post.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 《侠盗猎车手 VI》的英文简称。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A conversation conducted by speaking through an app or online service.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 通过应用或在线服务进行的语音聊天。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Here, receive a generated website in response to instructions given in chat.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 这里指在聊天中发出指令后，收到系统生成的网站。

slang_glossary.definition_en: In the praise phrase “really cooked,” did an especially good job or produced something impressive.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在「really cooked」这种夸赞用法中，意思是「干得漂亮」或「做出了很厉害的东西」。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Here, likely a playful invitation to try the mentioned tools hands-on in Replit.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 这里很可能是俏皮地邀请大家在 Replit 上亲手试用提到的工具。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Total addressable market, an estimate of the total revenue opportunity if a product captured all demand in its defined market.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 可服务的总体市场规模，指产品若覆盖所界定市场的全部需求时，理论上可获得的收入规模。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A visual or structured overview of a market that groups companies, products, or segments.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 市场版图，按公司、产品或细分领域梳理市场格局。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A company's highest-ranking executives, whose titles often begin with Chief, such as CEO or CFO.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 公司最高层的管理团队，成员职位通常以「Chief」开头，例如首席执行官或首席财务官。
